page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the legacy n1 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 45 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused tests, the server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 3374.03 and a Geekbench single-core score of 926.0, both falling into the weak or poor categories. Multi-core performance is similarly constrained, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 2941.66. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these limitations, with a PassMark encryption score of 1338.88 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.99 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-4 is its highly constrained memory capacity of 1.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for compute-bound tasks that do not require substantial RAM. It is suited for lightweight, CPU-bound workloads such as basic web serving, where it demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 2.92 GB/sec, or simple Redis key-value operations, achieving 2.8 million SET operations per second. It is not suitable for modern large language model inference or memory-heavy database deployments.
